Dividends paid to family members are often taxed at the lowest (or zero) personal income tax rates. In contrast, an individual on a salary that provides financial support to a child in university would be doing so out of after-tax income, that in the middle to upper income tax brackets would have typically been taxed in the 40% to 50% range.

This zero or low taxation of dividends paid to family members is the unfairness at the root of these tax changes.
